utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Mladen Naletilic and Vinko Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Before we have the witness, there is a schedule announcement. We have some changes in the scheduling of this case. On the 17th of September, Tuesday, we will sit in the morning instead of in the afternoon. On the 23rd of September, Monday, we will sit in the afternoon instead of in the morning. Having said that, Madam Usher, could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Stringer: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Please sit down. Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you know the name of Drazen Galic as someone who had been a member of the ATG Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't hear a response in English. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Vinko Skrobo during the same time that you were a member of the unit, more or less?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while, for a short while.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to direct your attention now to October of 1993. Actually before I do that, I want to just clarify one issue. From my notes yesterday, it indicated that you were a member of Mr. Martinovic's unit for approximately five months. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you leave the unit then -- well, if you'll just allow me to count, correct me if I'm wrong, it seems to me you joined the unit in perhaps the middle of May, shortly after the events of 9 May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ten or 15 days after the 9th of May, that is when I joined the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So then counting ahead forward five months from that point, that would take us to June, July, August, September, October of 1993. Can we then conclude that you left the unit sometime in October of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: More or less. Could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the time you left Mr. Martinovic's unit, did you remain in Mostar or did you return to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remained in Mostar. I signed a professional contract with the 2nd Guards Brigade of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then you moved into a different unit of the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what reason did you leave the Vinko Skrobo unit, given your fondness of Mr. Martinovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because this unit was a professional unit, that is when I was with Martinovic's unit, it wasn't a professional unit, because I had a rifle that I'd bought myself. I didn't get it from that unit. So I moved over to a unit which was -- which was structured as a proper army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the 2nd Guards Brigade was your commander Stanko Sopta?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you deployed, then, as a member of the 2nd Guards Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reconnaissance and sabotage company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where was that located? What was your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Action beyond the enemy lines, reconnaissance, things like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you based in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you leave the ATG Vinko Skrobo because you grew uncomfortable with certain conduct of its members?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it about the unit which led you to believe it was not a professional unit, such as the 2nd Guards Brigade? How did the units differ?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Skrobo ATG, we did not have enough of the military gear. We did not have uniforms. I repeat, I had with me the rifle that I'd bought myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe, sir, yesterday, you it testified that you had sufficient ammunition to carry out your duties on the front line; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the ammunition is not the only thing that a soldier needs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the 2nd Guards Brigade was a better-equipped unit than your unit which was manning the front line in Mostar? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the very early days of the war, we had no army whatsoever. So we started the war completely unprepared, and in time, the armament got better so this 2nd HVO Brigade basically that was the first proper army unit that I was with. Those before it were volunteer units which were neither properly trained, nor properly armed, nor anything. So that Mr. Martinovic's unit was made of the guys which were -- came from the street. That is friends, pals. We knew each other from before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on your observations as a member of the unit, did that lead to difficulties in terms of command, control and discipline within the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, perhaps you could put it that way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Certain members of the unit failed to act as correct and proper soldiers in carrying out their duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps there were things of that kind, but I couldn't really say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Having remained then in Mostar, I want to direct your attention to November of 1993. Were you aware of, or did you hear of, an incident in which a member of the Convicts Battalion was abducted from the military police station in Mostar? I'm sorry, let me state that again because I said it wrong. Were you aware of an incident in November of 1993 in which members of the Convicts Battalion came and abducted an HVO soldier, took him out of a military police station in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I object to this question. I think it goes beyond the scope of the direct examination and these questions relate to the Convicts Battalion, whereas the witness said that he belonged to quite a different unit, that is the Vinko Skrobo ATG.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I've never heard about it, I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, I think the Prosecution is entitled to ask this question because this witness was in Mostar area at that period of time, and I believe the Prosecutor will give some evidence about the relation between the Convicts Battalion and the Vinko Skrobo ATG, but anyway, the witness has answered this question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I want to direct your attention now to the events of 17 September, 1993. And maybe just to keep it flowing, I'll ask the Registrar to give you at this point a photograph, the one you saw yesterday, which is Exhibit P14.15. And I think it would probably be best if we could work with a clean copy in addition to the one that the witness marked on yesterday. If we could put first the one on the ELMO that the witness marked on yesterday? Okay. Witness, you said yesterday that you worked on shifts. What was your shift on the 17th of September? When did you arrive from your home or your parents' home in order to assume your duties on the front line? What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I had to make guesses about what happened on the 17th of September. You have to remind me. I don't remember -- I don't retain in my memory the dates so well. I can't really know what happened then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified about an incident in which a tank moved down from --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yeah, fine, fine. I see, yes. Yes. I'm aware of that day with the tank but I'm not -- I wasn't aware of the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know if that testimony from yesterday relates --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just. I want to clarify this. Let me finish.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, no, no. We don't -- there is a misunderstanding. I'm well aware of the incidents with the tank because I was at the front line that day but I don't know whether it was exactly on the 17th, but I believe you, if you tell me that it was the 17th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you speak English?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: A little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems to me that you're able to understand my questions directly without waiting for the interpretation, and as a result, you sometimes begin your answer before I finished asking my question. So if I could just ask you, remind you, as Mr. Par did yesterday, if you could try to break, give the interpreters a pause in between the question and answer so that they can do their job. Okay. Well, I want to talk about the day that you've described in which the tank was involved. And again, just to be certain, you don't know whether this is the 17th of September or not? It's a date -- you recall the incident but not the date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this day, what time did you arrive at the front line to begin your duties as a member of the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, some sort of operation was conducted on that day. Who briefed you about the operation and what your function was going to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: My immediate superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his name again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bobo Peric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was one of the four group commanders within the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's the location where the briefing took place? Where were you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the headquarters in the command of our unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that the place that's located on the Kalemova Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this the place where you would see prisoners working, I think you testified yesterday about doing work on automobiles. Is this where those prisoners were?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is this where Mr. Martinovic could usually be found?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that you were being briefed at the headquarters, did you become aware of any prisoners who had arrived from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: They all came from the Heliodrom, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the objective of this operation? Let me -- I reviewed your testimony from yesterday. It was my understanding that the objective of this operation was to, in fact, move across the Bulevar and to take positions on the far side or the eastern side of the Bulevar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any other units involved in this operation on the 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these were units that were conducting their own activities within their own areas of responsibility, perhaps along the length of the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within your unit, was it simply your shift that was going to take part in this operation, or did additional members of your unit come in to take part in the operation on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole unit, all the shifts, as far as I know, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did that include the members of the unit who were foreigners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there probably were, but I'm not sure, but probably yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were a rather small number but a number of mercenaries who were also members of the Vinko Skrobo unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were a few foreigners, but now, whether they were mercenaries, I'm not sure I would call them that. Perhaps a better name for them would be adventurers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Dinko Knezovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only superficially but I've heard about him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he a member of the Vinko Skrobo during this period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if he did driving for the unit, specifically bringing in prisoners from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout the war, I was on the front line, so I wouldn't know such individuals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That morning, when you were at the headquarters, you said that you assumed prisoners were brought in from the Heliodrom. So based on your having been at the headquarters, would you know whether it was Dinko Knezovic who was bringing in, transporting the prisoners from the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, but I couldn't state that for sure. I really don't know. I think the best thing is to say that I don't know because that was the actual answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see Mr. Martinovic in the headquarters on the morning when you were getting briefed about this operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably saw him. I can't quite remember but there is no reason that I wouldn't have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Mr. Takac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember him. He was on the front line, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he at the headquarters earlier, at the time that you were receiving your briefing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume that he was. Most probably he was. But I can't remember. Most probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall what time of day the attack or the operation was scheduled, was supposed to begin?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly it was going to be in the morning, but I do not -- I cannot remember the hour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I suggested to you that this was all going to take place at 12.00 noon, would that be correct or possible or not possible?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is maybe possible, but according to what I can recollect, it should have been in the morning but it is possible it would have been at noon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, at the briefing, at the headquarters, did you learn at that time that a tank was going to arrive in order to support your movement across the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tank arrived when I was already on the front line so I was on the front line at the time when the tank arrived.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I understand. I'll try to make my question more clear. Previous to that, when you were still in the headquarters getting your briefing, were you informed in the briefing that a tank was going to be involved in this operation in order to provide support for your advance across the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: They probably told us this but I can't quite remember. They most probably said it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You weren't shocked later on when a tank arrived at that location, at the time that the operation was going to begin, I take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, on the ELMO we've got the photograph that you were marking on yesterday, and just a couple of questions about that now. It's my understanding -- well, just to continue on, the briefing was concluded and I take it, then, that you and other members of your unit moved from the headquarters then down to the confrontation line, the area of the health centre; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And I believe yesterday you testified that you, your position was on the ground floor of the building you marked as building number 1 on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, but I was also -- I moved about in other places as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For now let's talk about the period of time prior to the arrival of the tank. During that period of time, were you inside the building, outside the building, or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I can recollect I was probably inside the building, but I wasn't in one place all the time. I was walking about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Walking about inside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's my understanding that certainly these windows that we see facing the confrontation line, those were blocked with sandbags; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you're inside the building, is it possible to see outside the building, either toward the confrontation line or north toward what used to be called Liska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. How were you able to see outside, then, from inside the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the building on the side opposite to where the front line was, normally wasn't protected, and it was possible to see extremely well how a tank was arriving. But it is only towards the front line that the sandbags were positioned with small openings for rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just want to be clear. Were you able to see outside of the building from the side that faces the sandbags that were across Liska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was able to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in this photograph, you made a line indicating the position of the sandbags. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it is a line which appears to extend out to the left from the side of the health centre, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then behind the sand bags you've made some --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought the witness could maybe show us this so that we can be absolutely certain about which line we are talking about so that we can be specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's a good idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It is a good idea.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, here were the bags, sandbags were positioned in this location that I'm just indicating.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then behind the sand bags you've made markings indicating what to me sounds like a big screen where carpeting was hanging from a cable across buildings that would have obstructed the view of anything behind; is that correct? Like a big, huge curtain across the street.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the height of the sandbag fortifications? How tall was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps two metres, perhaps a metre and a half.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tall enough so that a person could walk behind the sandbags without having to crouch down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that the person may have had to bend down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What time did the tank arrive, if you are able to recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly in the morning, but perhaps it is around noon, like you said. Maybe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a T-55 tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many crew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume there were three of them. It's just an assumption. I have never been in a tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position, were you able to see any of the crew members or were they inside the tank? As opposed to perhaps sitting up on top of the turret?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the tank crew is normally inside the tank during a combat operation. It would be completely stupid if they were sitting on top of the tank. When they finished their combat operation, which was very short, they returned and they stopped behind the building which I marked as under number 1, and they said that the tank was broken, not functioning any more, that it had been hit by sniper, that the optical sight was hit by a sniper. Perhaps this was the truth but perhaps they had a reason. Perhaps they didn't feel like fighting. I really don't know but maybe it fired two or three shells. That was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your position when the tank arrived behind the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was on the ground floor of the building, of the building under number 1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you preparing then to move outside and to move forward across the confrontation line, as had been planned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday that at some point, in fact a number of your comrades did move outside, I think toward the fountain. I had the impression that you remained inside the building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who is translating, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So others then went outside in the direction of the fountain, which is obviously toward the Bulevar, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your position inside the building, it seems to me that your view of what's happening forward of the sandbags, would have been largely obstructed. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, but I was not all the time in one place. I was walking. If you go back ten metres, you could see everything very well. There is a bunker right next, left -- on the left-hand side of the building and that's exactly where I was, for instance, in that location. There was a bunker left from the building number 1. It is easy to come from the centre of the building there. It's only ten metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you take the pointer and show us the position of this bunker, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: [indicates] Precisely where I am holding the tip of the pointer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this is a position just forward of the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction next to the sandbags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the enemy positions on the other side, it's my understanding, sir, that the Armija soldiers who were your targets were positioned in the basement of the buildings immediately opposite the Bulevar. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you take a pointer and indicate for us the buildings or the positions of the ABiH soldiers at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here. I am pointing at it with the pointer. Here the destroyed buildings, the destroyed buildings that I'm indicating with the pointer, this whole line here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you -- could I ask you to take the other clean photograph and put a circle around those buildings, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so the plan was for you and your colleagues to move across and to hopefully capture the positions that are within the circle that you just made; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the tank was to provide support for you in advancing across and taking those positions, I take it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Something like that. It's not quite accurate but let's say that that is it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I know that in military operations the plan usually doesn't unfold as you would always hope or expect but that was generally the idea? Is that a fair statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question. I don't understand it. I'm just an ordinary soldier and I find this too complicated. I really don't know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, and I wrote this down from reading your testimony, you testified that the objective was to cross over with the support of the tank. And can we agree that that was the objective?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I take it, then, that the tank's targets would have been ABiH soldiers positioned in the basement of these buildings that you've described or that you've circled?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems to me from the way you've described the conduct of the tank driver that they were in fact supposed to move past the sandbags closer down to the confrontation line but that they failed to do that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll have to repeat the question one more time, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it envisioned that the tank would move beyond the sandbags closer to the Bulevar, in supporting the infantry movement across the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you what my assumption was. The tank was supposed to get to the sandbags and to fire towards the cellars which is where I presume the enemy soldiers were. That was the only thing that the tank was supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's your view, then, sir, that the tank and the turret of the tank, having come up directly behind the sandbags would have been able to lower its turret over sandbags of 1 and three-quarters to two metres in order to fire on the basement of the buildings opposite on the Bulevar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my assumption. That's what I expected it to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I object to this type of question that's asking the witness to speculate. There have been already a few questions like this in relation to what the tank was supposed to do, what the witness thought the tank was supposed to do. The witness is -- was simply -- is simply now drawn into an area of questioning where he can not give good quality answers. He's saying, "I assume, I presume. I think this should have been the case." I don't think these questions are good. I think the only thing the witness could be asked is what he actually saw. But what the tank was supposed to do, what the tank crew was supposed to do, that's beyond his knowledge. So I object to the questions that are asking the witness to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I briefly respond? The witness was briefed about the operation. I think it's reasonable to expect the witness would have been provided information, not only about his own tasks, but the type of support he would have received in conducting the operation. So I think they are fair questions. He was present and I think he's in a position to give us information about what the tank was doing, what it was supposed to do, what it didn't do, and what its targets were. That's all I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. But it seems to me that this witness provided us with a very little knowledge of what actually the tank was doing at that time, and one thing we want to understand is that whether the sandbags blocked the view or blocked the gun of the tank at that particular point, because we heard some witness who said that in this direction. Would you please ask a question about -- in this direction?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to put Judge Liu's question to you, but first, before I do that, let's establish if you can give us an approximate -- an estimation, the distance between the position of the tank and the buildings that were the tank's target on the other side of the Bulevar. What's the distance there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: 30 metres, let's say 40 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that if the sandbags -- isn't it true, sir, that the sandbags were at such a height that they would have been too high for the tank's turret to target those positions, particularly the basement of those positions, from such a close distance, while it's positioned behind a wall of sandbags that's either one and three-quarters or two metres high?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sandbags were piled one on top of the other without any things in between, without -- it was very -- without them being stuck together. So it was very easy to knock them over. So the tank could have been firing anywhere on the basements wherever it wanted to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it would have been necessary to remove at least some of the sandbags so that the tank could fire on its targets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps one or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, another question, and then -- and directing your attention back to the photograph here, and maybe I could ask you to place a marking on this photograph again that shows the position of the sandbags, just so that we've got that. You've marked the sandbag position on the first photograph. Could you just put it in the same place on that one so that we ...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, again, setting aside the angle or the inclination of the turret of the tank, it seems to me, sir, that from that position, the tank's -- the ability of the tank shooter to position the turret horizontally would have been extremely limited by the fact that the health centre and the building across the street were next to it. It seems to me quite impossible for the tank to hit most of the positions that you've circled from the position behind the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object. This is not a question. This is an argument.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: I object to the form of the supposed question. It's not a question, it's simply argument. It's argumentative in nature. This witness has said he's never been in a tank. He doesn't know anything and it's speculation. But the form of the question is not a question. I object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Meek, I think the question asked by the Prosecutor is what we want to know. Witness, you may answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that I assumed that the tank fired on to the basement. That's what I expected. I expected the enemy soldiers to be in the basement. But to be honest, I don't know where the tank hit. I know that it fired two or three times. Perhaps that was the reason that the tank returned. Perhaps the crew saw that they couldn't hit. But this would be slightly longer story. They were not only in the basement, the enemy soldiers. They were also behind the building. If you hit the wall from this building, this derelict building with a grenade, with a shell, this wall could fall on to the enemy soldiers, which are behind it. It happened on one occasion, it happened that the wall of this building just fell, just like that, by itself, and we heard that somebody was calling for help from the enemy side. It was probably because of the rain that the wall became damp and then it became -- it was easy for it to fall. So I suppose the tank could have aimed at the basement or perhaps something else. I don't know. But I really don't understand what you're trying to achieve with this kind of questions, Mr. Prosecutor. Perhaps it couldn't hit the basement but ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me try to ask it a little more clearly. Looking at the circle that you made around the enemy positions, and moving outs to the buildings located on the extreme right of the circle, can you put the pointer on those? A bit closer to the -- the structure, yeah. It seems to me that it would have been impossible for the tank to shell those positions; is that correct, from its position behind the sandbags, it would have been obstructed by the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a few metres of the building could not be hit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me what part of the building could have been hit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I mark it or? [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've just made a marking on this photograph, putting lines through a part of the circle you marked previously. Is it your testimony that these are all areas that the tank would have been able to hit from its position behind the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, it seems to me --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I guess. I guess. That's a -- it is more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I just have a quick moment, please, to consult?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, and Mr. Stringer, we have spent a lot of time on that point. I hope you come to the next subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar to replace this photograph with the other one marked on by the witness yesterday?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, isn't it true that the position of the tank, according to your testimony, was at all times on the side of the health centre and that because of the position of the health centre the tank would not have been able to hit virtually any of the position that is you've just marked on this other photograph? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: You'll have to repeat the question, please. I wasn't really focusing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Looking at the position of the sandbags as you've marked it on your photograph from yesterday, if the tank remained behind the sandbags sir, isn't it true that the health centre, the structure of the health centre would have obstructed and prevented the tank from firing on virtually all of the positions that you've just marked in the other photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The building is not obstructing the view, but it will be simpler to see if you had given us the ground plan, because from this angle, when the photograph was taken from this angle, then you do not get quite an accurate, a completely accurate picture of the positions. So I'm again making assumptions. Now, whether I went wrong a metre or maybe two, I don't know how big an error that is. It could be an error that -- I'm professionally an engineer, so I suppose I should also been a better draftsman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, now that we are talking about the health centre structure, whether it is an obstruction or not, I think it is important to say that what we see on this photograph does not show the health centre building as it was at the time, so that first should be made clear and then ask the witness what kind of a building was there, how tall was it, and was it obstructing the view then? This is a photograph made with a new building there and we cannot really discuss a situation way was completely different. But anyway the Prosecutor has the photographer of the old health centre and let us use that and with that old photograph, perhaps we shall be able to see whether it was possible or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, you are giving testimony by yourself. All we want to hear is the answer from this witness. If there is great changes in the structure of the health building, the witness will tell us about it. And Mr. Stringer, I've already said that we have spent so much time on this point. I think it's time for you to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's my last line of questioning and it happens that we do have an old photograph in the courtroom that may be of -- of a bit of assistance, if I could ask the Trial Chamber's indulgence to very briefly show this photograph to the witness, it may assist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask the Registrar, it this is marked 14.20. I don't know if Mr. Par has seen it. You may want to show it to him first. If you could put this on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, if you could take a moment to look at this photograph, orientate yourself, does this appear to more closely resemble the conditions in the vicinity of the health centre, the fountain, during the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is even worse. The best thing would have been if you had brought a ground plan, that is a view from above.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On this photograph --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because you know, in that case, one could see what a tank could aim at and what it couldn't aim at.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mark the structure of the health centre on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It seems to me from the other photographs that you've made, that the line of sandbags was to some extent back from the edge of the health centre on Liska Street. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat it, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The line of sandbags was extending from a point of the health centre structure across Liska Street. That is to say the line of sandbags was not forward of the health centre. Rather it was back along the side of the health centre. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were next to the health centre but two or three metres forward. Now, let me repeat it. So, no, let's do it this way. Now, I'm pointing at the health centre. The sandbags were from this line in that direction, or perhaps a metre or two forward. This part which I am pointing at now was our bunker. This is a transverse wall and one or two metres forward and I know it very well because that is where I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were wounded in the bunker?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The bunker was forward of the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, behind them, a metre or two. Or perhaps flush with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that it's time for a break. We will break until quarter to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, let's start with the time when you went to join the 2nd guards Brigade. What does it mean a professional unit? Does it mean that somebody who joins that unit needs to sign a contract with it, a professional contract?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it means. I signed my first contract for three years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And does that contract mean that you are to get pay from that unit, that it is a kind of full-time job, that during the three years you have a guaranteed livelihood, simply by the fact that you are a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time when you joined this professional guards brigade, was it exactly at that time that this brigade was formed and was it one of the first formations in the professional army in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, at this point I'm going to object to leading questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't see why it's a leading question. You may proceed, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And which year was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Late -- no, beginning of 1994.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So at that time, 1994, the war was already over. Were those ATGs already dissolved or about to be dissolved, all those ATGs like the Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I assume they were dissolved by that time but I'm not sure, I'm not really quite sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you went to join this guards brigade, what was that motivated you to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to resolve the -- my problems, problems of livelihood, of pay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you wanted to have the problem of livelihood solved. Was there any other reason for which you quit the Vinko Skrobo apart from that particular reason that you told us, that it was solving your economic status, your livelihood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the chief reason. Perhaps there were some others. But that one was the principal one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there were some others -- were there some -- was that other reason that those ATGs would be disbanded and that therefore you wouldn't -- there wouldn't be any room for you there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now, when you joined this guards professional brigade, were those ATGs dissolved meanwhile? The war was over, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The war against the Muslims was over and I suppose that these units were dissolved, yes, yes, yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you stay with this guards professional brigade as a professional soldier? Did you get your pay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let's go back to, if we can find a clean photograph, 14.5, if I have a clean copy, and could we then have it on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Why are you going to use a clean copy? The re-examination should be within the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted a clean copy, I do not know whether I should explain it now in front of the witness or perhaps the witness should leave the courtroom for a while. But I want to use a clean copy because I want to establish once again where those sandbags were because there is something I would like to point out at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I'd like to add something to what I said before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to any re-establishing the positions of the sandbags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, our suggestion is that you use that copy marked by the witness during the cross-examination, and if you want to make a clarification of certain points, you are entitled to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we then have one of the previous 14.5 documents? That is the one on which the witness marked the sandbags and explained their location. Yes, you can leave this one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's begin with the tank. So you were asked several times by the Prosecutor and you answered what the tank was expected to do, what it was expected to target and so on and so forth. Now, my question is simple. All those answer that is you gave to the Prosecutor, was it your own knowledge or did you hear from somebody what the tank was expected to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know. I knew that the tanks was -- that the tank was to come.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But these answer that is you gave the Prosecutor in relation to what the tank was expected to do, was it the result of your assumptions or information that you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my wishes, what I thought that the tank should do, that is my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did anyone ever that day or on the eve of that day, explain the task that the tank was to have that day, what it would target, where it would go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody did. All I knew was the tank was to come. That is all that I knew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's look at this photograph and these markings. Can you please explain to me, not to me but to everybody in this courtroom, which path, which way did you use to come to the front line? Will you take the pointer up and show us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would take this path here, between the buildings where I am just pointing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, when you came there, you mentioned a cord, you mentioned a cable strung above the Liska Street. Where was it? Where is it on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll tell you approximately. I think that it was between these two buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you then draw it there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry, I was -- I went slightly wrong. I think I should push it two or three metres back, somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And mark it. Put, for instance, S, so that we know that it's a cord.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: That is "sajla" in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this cord, this cable was there, what was its purpose? What was there on it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some carpets hanging from it so that the snipers -- so that the snipers from the opposite side could not see men pass by.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how high was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Seven, eight metres, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Seven, eight metres. So the visibility was nil, one couldn't see?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, after that cord, you come across another obstacle, that is the sandbags, and where are they, these sandbags in relation to the cord?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my earlier testimony, I forgot to mention that there was yet another row of sandbags between these two buildings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, then, draw them now then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that is where there was another row of sandbags. So this tank, when it came up, at which particular row of sandbags did it stop?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those next to the -- no, no, no, next to the second row, those that are in front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far did it get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, where I showed the first time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here, we heard several testimonies showing that the tank was next to the first row of sandbags. Can you now positively state?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't really positively state it because I was inside the building, but I mean it was judging by the sound that I concluded it was quite near me but.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is what I'm trying to establish quite precisely because my impression was that you in your testimony, that you base your testimony on some assumptions and we want you to clearly tell us what you assumed and what you really saw for the Court. Can you tell us positively whether you saw or whether you recall next to which sandbags did the tank fetch up? If you're not sure, then tell us so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: When, that is better for me not to say anything because I'm not really sure, then it's better for me not to say anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But would you allow that it was possible for the tank to be next to the upper, to the second row of the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I object to the form of that question, Mr. President, and I move that the witness's answer be stricken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par. I think it's a leading question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Then I'll ask the witness something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, can you tell us positively today, next to which sandbags the tank exactly fetched up or can't you tell us that? Can you --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no, I can not be definite.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are you sure that there were some sandbags up there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, I'm quite sure that there were some sandbags up there. In my earlier testimony I simply did not think it was all that important, and to be quite frank, I mean, I don't really understand these questions about the sandbags. Why should it be all so important? There were the sandbags surely, the ones that I omitted and I'm sorry that it happened but, yes, there were -- they were there and other witnesses will confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I just for a moment -- may I consult my client, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. [counsel confers with client]

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No more questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from Judges? Judge Clark. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, first of all, this is probably a little personal but it helps the Judges, I think. You described where you used to live before the war and what happened to your home, and where you now live. Have there been any people in your position who have been able to go back to the area - I don't want to identify it - where you originally had your family home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm being deliberately evasive because I don't want to identify you or where you came from, but knowing your ethnic background and where your family used to have their family home, which was destroyed just before the 9th of May, 1993, what I'm asking you is: Has nobody in your position been able to go back to that same area now that the war is over?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area where I had lived before, there are not many Croats. There is nobody to return there, except me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I see. If you wanted to return, would it be a possibility or a probability?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not return there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I see. Now, if I could go on to some questions in relation to this case, I'm a little confused about your career during the war. You described to us how you were inducted into the HVO, that you had no choice about it, you were conscripted, and then you described your disenchantment with the HVO and you joined Mr. Martinovic's unit. How was that permitted, that one could just walk away from an army commitment and choose another unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, and not only in that town but throughout the area, there was a lot of confusion about. It wasn't stable. It wasn't like here in Netherlands. You can do certain things that wouldn't be allowed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So did you even have to get permission from your local commander to change over to what you described was a non-professional, voluntary unit? The Mrmak at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, probably out of politeness, I asked to be released, but I could have done without it, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: At the time in Mostar, following the 9th of May, was it possible for an able-bodied man, a man of military age, to walk freely through the town? Or did you have to go through checkpoints and show ID?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was a good thing to have a uniform, because there was a law on mobilisation at the time. I think there was. I assume there was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: So can I take it from that that there might be people who would stop you and say, "What unit are you with or what right have you got to be in this particular part of town?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably, yes, but it didn't happen to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Did you have an ID card when you belonged either to the HVO unit or to Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Would you have had two different cards or would the same card have done for your whole period before you joined the professional unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think they were different. I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Is it possible that you stayed with Vinko Skrobo for a little bit longer than October? And the reason I ask you this is that we've heard from witnesses who were part of the setting up of the new professional unit, that it was a little bit later than October that it was set up and I think your counsel agrees that it was really into 1994. So would you accept that you might be wrong about having left Vinko Skrobo in October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I moved to another unit, which then later on in its entirety transferred to the 2nd Guards Brigade. I didn't go directly. I didn't mention it because I didn't think it was that important, because at that unit where I had been, all the soldiers had decided to sign a professional contract.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: The reason I ask you this is that because we've seen documents in relation to other witnesses, and these documents have been presented on a number of occasions, and looking through those documents, we would see your name as being on the pay list of Vinko Skrobo on the 2nd of December, 1993. What would you say about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to state anything regarding the dates. It could be that date or it could be one month or two months earlier that I left the unit. I'm not sure. Perhaps our salaries were late. I wouldn't be able to say. I'm just assuming here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And when the time came for you to leave the Vinko Skrobo unit, how did you do that? Did you tell your unit group leader or did you go to Mr. Martinovic? Or did you just slip away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I told the group commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Now, if I can bring you to the events of the 17th of September, and you have answered very extensively in relation to that day, can I take it that it was a very unusual day, that there was an air of tension and fear and anticipation on that day compared with other days when you were at the front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It could be said, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: When you worked on different shifts, I take it that as a general rule, you worked with the same group of people, with the same group commander, so you would become very familiar with that group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could one follow from that logically that there would be members of different groups on different shifts that you would very rarely meet or might not meet at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were such, yes. We would meet them very rarely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Would it be possible for you to see people who were maybe on duty in and around coming off duty, coming on duty, as you were arriving or leaving your shift who might seem like strangers to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. It may be, I'm really not sure. Some people I knew very well. And some people I didn't know so well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Well, on the day of the 17th, a very special day when there was an attempt obviously to break through the confrontation line and to take some extra land, to move forward, you said that the whole unit was there and there were other units also. On that day, did you see people that -- or could you have seen people that you didn't know or didn't recognise?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't quite remember it that way. Most of the people I knew. Most of the people who were on the front line I knew. As far as I can recall. But these are details I cannot remember. The most important thing for me was to stay alive. That was my main point, my main idea because before the war I was a civilian I was not a professional soldier. So these are the things that I was thinking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Believe me, I can quite appreciate that. Before the tank actually engaged and fired -- I mean it would obviously have had to come from somewhere making a huge amount of noise. If you can recall that date, were you are instructions to exchange fire so that there was a lot of noise to distract the enemy's attention from the arrival of the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that, and I don't believe it to be so but I don't remember. I'm just an ordinary soldier. I can't answer these questions. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'm afraid I find that difficult to accept that you're an ordinary soldier. You were probably one of the best-educated men on the unit, and also you were a professional, civil engineer so your education would have given you, I believe, advantages. Do you recall, was there an exceptional amount of shooting before the tank arrived? If you don't remember, that's all you have to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. Really.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you remember if there had been any preparations for the arrival of the tank the day before? Was there any discussion about the use of the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there weren't much, but I don't remember. No, I really don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Do you have any recollection that there were fairly massive casualties that day for a small group of people on the front line? Do you have any recollection of that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the unit next to ours had several losses, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I'd suggest to you that it was more than several people who lost their lives. There were quite a lot of people. It means nothing to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by "quite a lot."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: I think it was more than two or three or four or five.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MP [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe, but I wouldn't know. I know there were losses. I know there were people killed but I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any questions out of Judge's questions? Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [no interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, thank you for coming here to give your evidence. When Madam Usher pulls down the blinds, she will show you out of the room. We all wish you a pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At this stage, are there any documents to tender, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I would propose to tender D2/44, that is the name and the surname of the witness and the seal. And then D2/45, the map that I used in the examination-in-chief, also under seal. D2/46, a photograph. 14.5. And the photographs probably -- what the witness marked on. Now, I don't know whether there is a number. I think that will be entered. I think these are the exhibits. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Those documents are admitted into evidence. Do you have any documents to admit, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we would offer the photograph 14.5 that was -- that the witness marked on during his cross-examination, and then also Exhibit 520.1 which he was shown yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about that photograph P14.20?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, I'd forgotten about that one, Mr. President. Thank you, the photograph 14.20 we also would offer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any objections, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I have no objections, but I object to P20 in relation to the objection that I -- 520, if that is the same document in relation to what I said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, we have already made a ruling yesterday, saying that we rejected those documents because of their late submission, not because of their contents. And in this document, in relation of this document, we have already admitted some other documents in this aspect. So we believe that this document is relevant to this case. So we decided this document is admitted into the evidence, as well as the document P14.5 and P14.20 are admitted into the evidence. It is so decided. Madam Usher, could we have the next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can hear you. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Examined by Mr. Par:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Before we start with the questions, I would like to tell you that the Trial Chamber has approved protection measures for you so your face and your name will be protected and all the data, information related to you personally. To start with, I will hand you a piece of paper on which your name is written. If this is correct, could you please just say yes? Don't read it aloud.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will try during the questions to speak as slowly as possible and to make pauses between my questions and your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, now I would ask to go into closed session for a few moments, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please tell us at the time of the Serbian aggression on Mostar, could you tell us what happened to you? Were you at the time a member of the army? How did you live through the Serb aggression on Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I was engaged in the reserve police until the reserve force of the JNA Army came, until the 14th of September, 1991. On the 16th of September, I joined the reserve force of the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you it tell me joined, were you mobilised? In what way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did that happen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I was not mobilised. I volunteered. I volunteered to join the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the reserve force of the police doing at that time? What were your duties? What were your tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The reserve force of the police did the same as the regular forces. We were checking the traffic and we were on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell us until when did you stay in the reserve force of the police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The reserve force, I stayed until the conflict escalated, when the aggression started, against Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Mostar itself was until about April.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason for you to leave in April, 1992, to leave the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: It was disbanded, the reserve police force was disbanded, was dissolved and we all volunteered to join the defence of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also personally join the defence of the town and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I joined the defence of the town. I volunteered and at that time I became a member of HOS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Which HOS unit? Where was it stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The HOS unit was there to defend the town, and it was from the territory of the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now tell us who commanded that HOS unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: It was commanded, that is the commander of HOS in Mostar was Vinko Martinovic, Stela.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Vinko Martinovic, Stela, before that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I knew him before the war because we lived nearby. We lived practically in the same neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on what kind of terms were you, what kind of relationship did you have with him? Were you acquaintances, friends, or what, before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, we knew one another. We simply came from the same neighbourhood, nothing much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you now briefly tell us about -- something about that unit, how strong was it, how many members did it have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That unit was like every other unit that defended the town. It could have been about 30, 40 men strong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that number increase or was it always the same?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, it increased or sometimes decreased. People came and went. To join other units at times.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember anything about the ethnic composition of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: In ethnic terms, there were Serbs and Croats and Muslims together because our goal was to defend the town against the aggression, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So tell me now what were the duties of the unit? What did you do specifically? Did you participate in any actions? What were your duties? What were the duties of the members of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, we guarded the bridges until they were blown up and then you know how it was. There was street combat between the buildings. So that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally participate with that unit in the fighting for the liberation of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about the name, about the reputation that unit enjoyed in Mostar, especially after the liberation from the Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, we were appreciated there highly because we went where others were reluctant to go. We usually went to places which were dangerous.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us now how long did you stay with that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I stayed with that unit until it was disbanded. I wouldn't know the exact date. I don't remember it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when that unit was disbanded, and when you left it, were you militarily engaged anywhere else apart from that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could Mr. Par also speak into his microphone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to join the battalion at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Two things to remind you. One, please make a pause between the question and the answers. Two, you are reminded to speak directly into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My apologies to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So after you left HOS, you joined that unit. Is it an HVO unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is an HVO unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was this unit stationed and what were your tasks there? What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Par please bring list microphone closer to him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
