utterances.text: Our unit was stationed at the Heliodrom. It was the old air force school of the Yugoslav People's Army. My duties were -- my duties in that unit because it was a mixed artillery battalion and our tasks were.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, we could not hear the end of the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 9th of May, 1993, the day when -- the interpreters are warning that they could not hear the end of your last answer, and that is the question where were you stationed and what were your duties. So I have to ask you to repeat your answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The unit was stationed at the Heliodrom. That was the former air base of the Yugoslav People's Army, and the air force school. My task Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 15150 to 15153. was, that is I was trained for anti-armoured operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The 9th of May, 1993, the day when the conflict between the Croats and Muslims started, find you there as a member of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of this mixed artillery battalion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now tell us briefly, that 9th of May, 1993, what happened to you personally? Will you tell us what you did that day, how did you see that day and the conflict that broke out that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: A day before that, I had a day off, and that morning, that is in the morning of the 9th of May I was to go to the Heliodrom, to the mix the artillery battalion. However, sometime early in the morning, that is at day break I heard gunfire and I couldn't understand. I was at sea. I didn't know what was happening because it was all calm before that. I came out to the balcony and I could see people running to and fro and there were some soldiers there, so I asked some people from the neighbourhood what's going on and they explained to us that the Muslims had launched an action and that they were advancing towards Rondo. And I don't know, I merely put on the uniform of my own will. I picked up the rifle, the one that I had, and I went out and joined those men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it happened at about what time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know. Sometime in the morning. I don't know. Somehow in the morning. That's when it was. The day was breaking. It was dawn.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And now with that group, you go -- you are moving towards the Rondo. That is towards the place from which the attack is advancing, and what do you do? What happens then? Is there any fighting? Where were you? Where -- how far did you manage to get?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: So we reached the Rondo, there were already some soldiers there, and yes, there was fighting there, so we joined in. We joined in this skirmish with the Muslim troops, and we gradually push them back towards the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you -- are you telling us that these units, and if I may put it that way, of the Muslim army had already penetrated into the depth, to the Rondo, or was is it that you clashed with them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We object to the leading question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it is a leading question because the witness answered gave us the same doubts about the response. Mr. Par, you may rephrase your question in some other way.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were saying that you had contact and fighting with the Muslim troops that day. Where did this fighting take place? Where was the front -- I mean the front line at which you were that morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That morning they had penetrated into a depth, perhaps as much as 15 metres from the Rondo, 10 to 15 metres from the Rondo, and that is where the fighting started and we were pushing them back towards the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the Rondo of course is near -- in the west -- on the west side of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness nods.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Now, did you manage to push them back? How much did you push them back? And what did you do then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The fighting lasted almost a whole day, and we managed to push them as far as the health centre, and several of them, several of them were in the health centre and they also retreated after our attack. They also retreated across the Bulevar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That morning, that day, around the health centre, did you see Vinko Martinovic, Stela, there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I didn't see him that day, and I couldn't see him because there was too much commotion and then fighting and action, so I couldn't see him. I didn't see him there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But later on, did you learn in some way where he was that particular day, that 9th of May, during the combat?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, no, not personally but I heard from others that he was somewhere there along that front line. Where exactly, I don't know but he was there and that he had participated in the -- in the action.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that day, that 9th of May, when did you first see Vinko Martinovic, Stela?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: After that 9th of May, after we had pushed back to the health centre and away from the health centre, across the Bulevar, then I saw him the next day, when things had calmed down a little, so I saw him the very next day, on the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So where was Vinko Martinovic, Stela, on that 10th of May? With whom was he and what were the circumstances under which you saw him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Why, we met somewhere there, between the health centre and Rondo. He was with some plain soldiers. He wasn't with anybody important, with people like we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after that 10th of May, after your encounter on the 10th of May, after that, did you have any contact with him? Did you used to see him after that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. We saw each other after that because we, who on that 9th of May, had embarked on the defence, that day we simply saw him, because we had put together a kind of a group, a small unit, nothing official, but we had a small group of sorts and we saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in the same group with him or did he have somebody else? Did you merge with his group or some other group? Will you please explain it to us? What do you mean when you say, "We formed a small group"? How did it come about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, it came about on a voluntary basis simply people got together. I don't know how to explain it. But at that particular point of time, none of us cared which unit each one of us belonged. All we cared about was how to push back the Muslim troops. And after that, we decided that each one on his own to quit the units that we had belonged to formerly and to join a new formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So you joined what is that formation, how strong is it? Who is its commander? Where are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That formation was 25 men strong, 20, 25 men strong, in the early days, our commander was Vinko Martinovic, Stela, and we had elected him of our own volition to be our commander, because he had already proven himself in the war against the Serb troops as somebody with authority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And where did this unit hold positions? Where was it stationed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That unit held positions in the area of the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, did this unit, and I'm referring to the 10th of May, and after it did it have any name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: At that time the unit didn't have any name officially but we, between us, called it Mrmak, after Stela's dog.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did it receive any logistic support from somebody, armaments, uniforms or anything to do with the military needs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. Right at the beginning, we did not enjoy any logistic support, because the unit was still in the process of being formed. So that these things were not yet put in proper place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did you remain with the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I remained with it until the very end of the war with the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to that beginning, to the very beginning, when you got together and stayed, during the time that you spent in the unit, what changed? Did the number of men in the unit grow up with time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, yes, the number of men increased, which is only natural. People came to the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how much?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, it grew up to be some 40, 45 men strong.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This unit, did it ever change the positions which it took initially next to the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. We never changed. We never moved to another position throughout the war against the Muslims, never moved away from the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it given any new assignments, apart from guarding the front line? Was it ever sent to some other actions possibly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, never. We never went anywhere. Our area of responsibility was only the health centre, and nothing but the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And over time, did the commander of the unit change or was it always the same person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no changes. Vinko Martinovic was the commander throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the unit change its name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. When the unit acquired a structure, then eventually we became -- we were given the name of Vinko Skrobo and we became an HVO unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say an HVO unit. Under whose command in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, the complete front line of the town defence was under the staff of the town defence. We were also put under the command -- under the command of the town defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So did you then begin to receive the logistic support and all -- everything that you needed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. We were getting all that we needed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now I'd like to show you a map, that is a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is a clean copy of 14.5, we would like to show it to the witness, because I have 14.4, which is almost identical but -- if not, then we shall use 14.4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. So we have before us photograph 14.5. It is an aerial photograph of a section of the Bulevar, and now, Witness, I want to ask you to look at the photograph and show us where were the positions -- where the positions of your unit were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The positions of my unit were strictly in the health centre. This is the health centre building, and that is where our positions were, within this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you now take a marker and make a circle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this building that you call health centre, will you put number 1?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Otherwise, what was there in this building, in this health centre? Were there certain positions, some guard posts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, that is where your positions and guard posts were, at certain points there were guard posts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us whether you had anywhere some reserve forces, some standby position where the soldiers would be waiting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, we did have a reserve, and they were in this building over there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you mark it with number 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, and where was your headquarters? Where was your command post?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The command post was, if you took this street, then a kilometre a kilometre and a half or 1200 metres towards the centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, tell me, this front line, was it fortified in some way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: This front line was fortified a little bit. Nothing much. And those were mostly the openings, that is holes in the walls that we had made ourselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We are talking about this building, about the health centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I'm talking about the health centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any protection, any shield, any screen, from sniper or other gunfire or were there any obstacles on the street which passes by the health centre, that is the Liska Street? Can you tell us something about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. There were some kind of -- there was some kind of protection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please show us where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, behind this building, behind the building which housed the reserve force, there, in this part of this street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what kind of protection was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: We had bags and garbage containers which had been placed across the street and above it we had a cord with carpets so that we were protected against the sniper fire when we were -- when -- on our way to the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you mark it also and put number 3 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And tell -- can you tell us which unit adjoined you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: To our right was the Benko Penavic unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you show us where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: They were here in this -- in this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: And on the other side, the units changed. I think every two or three days they took shifts. I can give their names if you want me to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we make a break now? Because I have finished with the map. I would like to move on to another subject. So perhaps this would be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will break here. We will resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Par. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I continue, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have to tell you that the interpreters have asked us to slow down when we speak, and perhaps speak a little more loudly. I was it particularly warned. And to make more breaks between questions and answers. So now you showed us on the map where the positions were and now perhaps you could describe for us what life in this unit was. What were the military tasks and so on? So perhaps it is in this area that we could then go on with a few questions. For instance, were you always in this unit? In which way it did you go on to carry out your tasks? If you can perhaps elaborate on the way that you were carrying out the tasks in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, we went for shifts on the line, support for the health centre. The shifts were eight to 12 hours, depending on the situation. On the security situation, whether attack was expected or whether there was an attack ongoing on our positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you mostly there around the health centre or in the command? Where particularly? You personally.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. Not in the health centre. Only when I had a shift there or when there were attacks, I was on the line. But as far as I'm concerned, I would just go normally home and I was then in my civilian clothes. There was no need for me ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you finished your shift did you have any other duties related to your unit or do you have any other supervision afterwards or were you only under supervision while were you in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: There was no supervision after we left the unit. It was only while we were reserve in the command or in the building that I indicated following that we didn't have any kind of supervision.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you would go for the shift, to carry out your duties on the line, on the front, what did it look like? Were there daily combat? What was your duties specifically in keeping the position, keeping the line, you as a soldier, during an ordinary day? What were you doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, we would stand guard. There were not attacks all the time. For instance, for ten or 15 days nothing would happen. There would be no attack. There would be a kind of lull in the fighting and so we would go around the guard posts and that was that. We were on duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it happen that on occasions there were larger scale clashes in the time period while were you in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: There were certain sabotage attempts by the Muslim army but we successfully managed to defend. They tried to break into our premises and to take the positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 17th of September, 1993, did you -- were you in that unit when there was a larger scale operation on that part of the front? And when, during that operation, there was a tank there taking part? Do you remember that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I was there on that day, during that operation, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please indicate on the map which is before you, where were you on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: On that day, during the attack, I was located in front of the building, behind the wall here, you can see a wall here, behind this small wall, in front of the health centre building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps briefly, in your own words, tell us what was this operation and what happened on that day on the front?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: It was an operation which was happening throughout the front line in the city, not just on the Bulevar. It also happened in other parts of the town. It was also ongoing in other parts of the town. The operation started and we went out into the front in all this chaos and shooting, I cannot give you specific details. I was just an ordinary soldier who was also sheltering and I was just peeking out to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were behind this wall. Did you go forward from that wall or did you go across the Bulevar? Did you go to the Bulevar? Or were you there all the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no. We didn't go anywhere forward. We stayed behind that wall. We didn't go forward. We didn't advance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why didn't you go forward? What were the reasons? Did you intend to go forward?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Our intention wasn't to advance. We thought that we would start to take part of the territory which would have been normal in military operations but we didn't go forward.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When this operation -- whether this operation was successful or not and how long did it take?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: This operation, I cannot tell you exactly. It didn't last very long because it wasn't successful and we were ordered to retreat, to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there casualties, were there loss, were there people killed in that operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: In that operation, there were no casualties. There was one person lightly wounded, nothing seriously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about other units? Were there perhaps people killed in other units? Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I heard that there were losses, people killed, on that day, from some other units, but I don't know these people so I couldn't tell you who they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this operation, did a tank join you in that operation? Do you remember that and if you do remember, could you perhaps tell us something about what this tank did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. In that operation, a tank took part, and what this tank did was just to fire one or, no, two shells, and then it withdrew.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, did you see or did you hear why would it retreat and why did it go back?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I saw why it went back. Its sight was damaged by sniper fire. It had been fired on by anti-armoured weapons and it had to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally see this damage or did you hear about this from someone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I didn't hear it from anyone. I saw it personally, because I served in the JNA in the armoured unit so I know what sights were and I know that the damage that it suffered, it was forced to withdraw, to retreat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you see that? Where was the tank exactly when you saw that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The tank was here, just in front of us, just by the wall here, and after two shells that it fired, it went right back along this way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When it returned, where were you -- where were you seeing this sight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Where the driver was or where the turret was, the sight was damaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in relation to your knowledge and to what you know about the sights, how did you know that, that it couldn't go any further?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I was someone who was operating the sight in such an armoured vehicle, so I do know that this tank could not be used without the sight.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us whether, around the tank, did you see any soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I didn't see any soldiers because that would have been certain death, if anyone found themselves near the tank because everything was open so it was -- it would be a mad thing to do, to go anywhere near the tank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On that day, at the time of the operation, did you see anyone in that part of the front line, who was a prisoner of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I did not see anyone. I did not see any POWs near the front line at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever heard that on that day, on that part of the front line, that prisoners of war were used as a human shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I told you earlier, near the front line, there was no prisoners of war. There were no prisoners of war, in that part where we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps hear that there was talk of some prisoners of war being used with wooden rifles going next to the tank, being used as human shield?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, never, no, I never saw that and I was there directly. Nobody was next to the tank. That would have been a mad thing to do, to be right there in the line of fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps tell anyone that this happened or that some operation of that kind was being planned, involving prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't tell anyone, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know a person by the name of Allan Knudsen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I don't know that person.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know either in the ATG unit Vinko Skrobo were there foreigners in that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, there were foreigners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember any of those foreigners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I remember an American, Tom, and I remember a German man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps some Danish men, somebody from Denmark?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who these foreigners were? How did they get -- end up in your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know who these people were. They probably came from the command of the defence of the town. They came and then they were put at the disposal of the units, not just in our unit but in units all along the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally have any contact with these foreigners? Did you speak to them in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I had contact with them, the only way, which was using my hands, like all the other soldiers who were there. Nothing special.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean, with hands? Why did you have to use your hands for these contacts? What were you trying to tell them on those occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: This was just using my hands to gesticulate, to show where a position was, where they are not supposed to go because of sniper fire. And that was that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in charge of contacts with these foreigners? Was this part of your tasks to tell them where to go and what to do?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no. That was not my task. Anybody from the soldiers could have showed them, could have told them what to do and how to take care of themselves.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there an interpreter in the unit, somebody who would have been able to interpret, to translate certain things that would have been necessary for them to know or for them to ask something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. There was no interpreter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did these foreigners perhaps understand Croatian?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Some of them perhaps understood a little or perhaps they could say a few words. That was all. Nothing else, nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you at the time speak a foreign language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: At that time, I didn't speak any foreign language. Perhaps a word or two but I didn't speak a foreign language, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I just ask a question in private session, Mr. President, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just before that day, 17th of September, 1993, did you speak to any of those foreigners about the operation that was coming up?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I did not speak to them, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on the eve of that, did you have any information whether there would be such an operation? And did you have any details before 17th of September?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: We didn't have any details. We knew that there would be an operation coming up but we did not know what kind of operation that would be. I was just an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here I have to put it to you that one foreigner, a Danish man, Allan Knudsen said that he spoke to you prior to the operation, one day before the operation, and that you were in informing him about this operation. Could you perhaps comment on this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I can comment on that. I never spoke to him about it, and what his reasons were that he said this, I really have no idea.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Did you know a foreign soldier by the nickname of Svabo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember a tragic event where a young boy was killed in relation to this man Svabo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I remember that, a young boy, I don't know how, found himself in his flat, died, was killed by a hand grenade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember whether police came or was there any action taken in relation to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: There was an investigation and follow this investigation, Svabo was dismissed from my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whose son that was, this young boy who was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I heard that this was a son of a certain man called Halil Lopata, I think. That's what he was called.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you personally know this Halil Lopata?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I did not know him but I heard that he was an alcoholic, that he was a man with problems.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I never saw him in the unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see him in the unit as a prisoner of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no. I told you I never saw him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the unit, Vinko Skrobo unit, were there prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: In our unit, no. All the prisoners who were prisoners of war were brought from Heliodrom. In our unit we did not have any prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean those who were brought from Heliodrom. Could you tell us what did these prisoners do in the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: They worked as car mechanics. Some of them were car mechanics who were working to fix our vehicles. They worked to fix ambulance vehicles. They were working on armouring these vehicles in order to protect them from fire.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These prisoners of war, where were they? Were they in the command building or somewhere else, in Kalemova Street or somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: These were in Kalemova Street, in the command building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you tell me, now that we see the photograph, where the prisoners of war ever brought anywhere near there? Were they brought?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Perhaps one or two, not more than that. And they came to this building, to this building of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me what did they do in this reserve -- building of the reserve force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: In that building of the reserve force, they came to tidy up, to clean a little, and that was that. And then they were returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, were they in any way in any danger from enemy fire? Were they working in any conditions that were putting them at risk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. They were not working in any dangerous conditions because the reserve force building was -- the reserve was in the cellar, in the basement of this building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Here in Kalemova Street, near the command, were they there at risk from fire or from anything else? Were they in any dangerous conditions there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, they could not have been put in any risk or they could not have been put in any dangerous position because the staff, the headquarters, was deep inside the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see or hear that a prisoner of war in that unit was injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no. That didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whether at any time you saw that any of these prisoners of war were physically mistreated or abused in any way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I never saw that, and nobody was mistreated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the conditions like for them? Where did they eat, the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The prisoners ate at the same restaurant where we ate, that is the restaurant Hladovina. They had the same meals as we did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether they had any possibility to receive visitors?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: They had possibility to receive visitors. They even went home.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what they did, were they worked and when they were fixing these cars, were they forced to do this or did they do this on a voluntary basis? Were they paid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: They did it on a voluntary basis because we gave them good conditions, good living conditions. Even some of us, we gave them money for what they did. They had cigarettes. I don't know whether in other units they would have had the same good conditions as they had in our unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did some of the prisoners sleep there perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. There were a couple of them who slept there, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there a reason? Do you know why they would stay there overnight?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Simply they would spend the night there, they could have gone home but they would spend the night. They perhaps worked late or something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you know a prisoner of war by the name of Nenad Harmandzic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I did not know that name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I see the name appears correctly in the transcript, Mr. President, so I don't have anything to say. I thought I heard it differently over my headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. You may continue, Mr. Par.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, your unit, did it ever take part in expelling Muslims from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. My unit never did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally, did you personally expel anyone from an apartment? Did you force anyone out of an apartment? Or do you know that any of your soldiers did that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I never did that and I don't know that any of my soldiers ever did that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you hear that there are stories around Mostar that Stela and members of his units took part in the expulsions of people from flats and in looting? Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I heard about that from stories, from people, that there were a lot of false representations of this, and I even heard it from a lady. I was a member of this unit, and this lady came to tell me that she was expelled from her apartment, that she was robbed. And then I asked her who did that and she said that this was Stela and his men who did that. I asked her, "What did they look like," so I could know who these people were, and she said, "Stela is tall and dark," which is not at all true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell Stela about this event? Did he know about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I did tell him about it and we tried to somehow get to these people, to find them, to trace them, but we never managed to do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: According to your recollection, in that part of the front line, in front of the health centre, were there Muslims who were crossing from one part of the town to another? Did you ever see any such occurrences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of cases were there? Was this en masse or was this individual cases?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, they were not crossings en masse, these were just people who were crossing because they had families over there so they wanted to be with their families, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did it look like in real life? How did they cross over and get away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, we would call out to the other side because it was a very small distance, only across the street, so we would call out to them and ask them to stop firing, to stop any action so that people could get through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it also apply to the other side?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It did. Croat families or people on their own would cross over in the same way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was it the same principle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, it was the same principle, some kind of a local ceasefire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we go -- may I just consult my client for a second?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I have concluded with this, my examination. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination? Any cross-examination, I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. Cross-examined by Mr. Stringer:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could ask the Registrar if we could either push the ELMO back just a little bit so that I can see the witness and he can see me? That's better. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, just a couple of questions first of all, about the HOS unit that you were a member of during 1992. I think you testified that you joined the HOS unit that was commanded by Mr. Martinovic in approximately April of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: 1992, that is when I said the conflict started, and I joined perhaps a little later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The liberation of Mostar happened in June of 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And both HVO and HOS units were involved in this action which liberated Mostar from the Serbs; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the liberation of Mostar, then tension arose between the HOS and the HVO about which unit would be perhaps play a greater role in the area and in controlling Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I know nothing about that. I was just a foot soldier.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know Blaz Kraljevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Not personally. I saw that man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was from Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know where he came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was killed with other members of his party, assassinated outside of Mostar in August of 1992, do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this period of time, is it true, sir, that a significant number of Serb residents of Mostar were evicted and driven out of the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as you know, sir, the same Serbs continued to live in your area of town throughout April and throughout the summer of 1992? No changes at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. There were no changes at all. They lived there normally. They even fought side by side with us in the units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Serbs then, just so we are clear, then, sir, say in 1994, the same number of Serbs were living in Mostar as had been living there in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Will you repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the Serbs living in Mostar -- I'll rephrase it: Did the Serbs living in Mostar in 1991 and 1992 experience any difficulties as a result of what you called the Serb aggression?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. Ordinary people, civilians, no, they had no difficulties at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you joined the HVO and testified that you were first a member of what you called a mixed military battalion. I think you were involved in an anti-artillery; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I said it was a mixed artillery battalion and that I was trained for anti-armoured operations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were based at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. We were based at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your unit a part of a brigade or a battalion of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: At that time, we were a mixed artillery battalion. I wouldn't know under which battalion we were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were a member of this unit on the 9th of May, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I was a member of that unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That man, that man's name was Slaven Knezovic, of that part of my unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, I think you testified, you heard the sound of gunfire, the sound of armed conflict, and you then set out and joined up with members of what later became the ATG Vinko Skrobo, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. That is not correct. I did not say that I joined the unit, but people from that neighbourhood, people who had been members of other, different units, we of our own volition went to the Rondo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time you went to the Rondo, Witness, you were aware that there was a full-blown conflict taking place between units of the HVO and units of the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Not at that particular time. I wasn't aware that it was a major conflicts. Belief me, I did not think about it being a big, major conflict. The only thing that mattered me was to repulse that attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Instead of reporting to your unit, you instead linked up with Mr. Martinovic or some of his associates at the Rondo, is that what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. That is not what happened. I went with a couple of friends, with people I knew from the neighbourhood, and I couldn't report to my unit because all the roads to my unit had been blocked. It was too dangerous to take any one of those paths, because I would have been killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who were some of the people that you joined up with then on that day, the 9th of May, at the Rondo? Do you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: They were my neighbours. Those who were there, who lived there in the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, were they in uniform? Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. They had uniforms and they were armed, like I was, because we were already members of the -- of HVO units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, any of those people that you joined with that day, did any of those other people subsequently become members of Mr. Martinovic's unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, but later on, not at the very beginning. In the beginning, they were not members of any unit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, in this trial, there has been evidence indicating that some number of Muslims were transferred from West Mostar to the Velez Stadium or directly to the Heliodrom where they were held for some ten days. Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I am.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There has been some testimony indicating that this was sort of a protective isolation or that these Muslims were put at the Heliodrom for their own safety because of the conflict. My question is whether you were involved in transferring Muslims from West Mostar either to Velez Stadium or to the Heliodrom at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I had no part in that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not on the 9th of May or the 10th of May or the 11th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because I asked that, Witness, because in fact you've been named by at least one witness in this trial as someone who was participating in those activities on the 9th of May, together with Mr. Martinovic. So I put it to you, sir, that in fact on the 9th of May, you, Mr. Martinovic, and others, were in fact moving Muslim civilians out of West Mostar toward the Heliodrom. Isn't that a fact?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. That is not true. Somebody invented this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Muslim people who were held then at the Heliodrom were subsequently released on more or less the 18th of May. Does that sound correct to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I know nothing about that. I really don't. I was on the front line. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd like the witness be shown Exhibit P456.1, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you're going to be shown an exhibit in this case, which is a report of the 1st Military Police Battalion in Mostar, dated 14 June, 1993. I should have informed, Mr. President, I informed counsel earlier, all of the documents that had been assembled for the previous witness, I'm going to use that same set of documents for this witness. Mr. President, I can offer to give the witness my version of the original-language document, if it would make things go faster.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, take a moment to read that document over. And perhaps if we could use this time, I'd like also to give the witness the map which is Exhibit P11.18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to read that document, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you seen the part where there is a reference to a report in which uniformed men had been rounding up Muslim civilians in the Dum block? A patrol was dispatched and Stela was found with approximately 40 well armed soldiers, expelling Muslims from their homes. This report again is for the 13th and 14th of June, 1993. Witness, the reason I draw your attention to this document is because the Trial Chamber in this case has heard testimony that you, in fact, were involved in expulsion of Muslims from this particular section of Mostar on the 13th of June. And so again, my question is, sir, whether, in fact, as indicated in this document, you, Mr. Martinovic and others were present in this section of Mostar expelling Muslims from their homes on the 13th and 14th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I've already said that we did not take part in any expulsions. We were on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness to be shown Exhibit P620.1.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Take a moment to read that document, Witness. Witness, do you know anything about an expulsion of Muslims from the Centar II neighbourhood of Mostar on the 29th of September, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a military police report, just like the previous one. My question is whether the military police would in fact have been in a position to know which units and individuals were involved in these sorts of activities perhaps better than you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot say, because I am just a foot soldier, whether they had this information, whether they did, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say you heard about this incident, I take it; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I've heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hear that Mr. Martinovic was involved in this activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I didn't, because Mr. Martinovic could not be involved in this activity, since we were not responsible for the town. We were responsible for the section of the front line called the health centre, and that was all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you it testified that after you finished your shift, then, you -- I believe you testified you would simply return to the place where you live; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Isn't it possible, sir, isn't it quite likely, in fact, that you would have not known about the whereabouts and activities of Mr. Martinovic and other members of the unit when you were off duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Could you repeat?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's likely, isn't it, that you would not know about the activities and whereabouts of Mr. Martinovic, certainly at those times when you were off duty?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, when I was off duty, I was usually at home, or at times I spent part of the day at the headquarters and Mr. Martinovic spent most of his time at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the end of this document, sir, there is a reference to Zlatan Jelic, also known as Mijo Jelic. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he in charge of the defence sector for Mostar town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. He was the commander of the defence of the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then underneath that name appears the name of Ivan Andabak. Do you know who is Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I know who Ivan Andabak is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he associated with the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified about occasions when there would be kind of an informal or a local ceasefire at which times, persons would cross the confrontation line. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you -- lets me ask you: These local cease-fires, were there times when these were arranged by soldiers on opposite sides of the confrontation line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I haven't asked you yet about Ernest Takac but do you recall that he was a member of the ATG Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I remember him. He was a member.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he go by a nickname of Brada?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall an occasion in August of 1993, when Mr. Takac made an arrangement with someone on the other side whereby a Muslim named Mujanovic was to be exchanged for a Croat who was being held on the east side of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. I do not remember an exchange. There were voluntary crossings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm specifically referring to an exchange of a person named Bojana Mujanovic, an exchange for a Croat named Stjepan Milicevic. Do you know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't. No, I don't know anything about that. Those names tell me nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could I ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First before we move on, perhaps, witness, just to refresh us all, could you take the pointer and point to the neighbourhood of Dum that was referred to in that first document that I showed you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: It should be here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I ask you to take one of the markers and just to put a -- perhaps a number 1 in the area of the quarter of town called Dum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then could you do the same thing in the area of Centar II neighbourhood that was referred to in the other document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. We can withdraw that exhibit and we are going to return to the photograph, 14.5, and I think I'm going to need a fresh one because I'm going to ask the witness to make one marking on it. Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, now we are going to talk about the date in which the tank was involved in that operation. Looking at that photograph, can you just take the pointer and show us what used to be called Liska Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: This was Liska Street.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the tank moved down Liska Street from the Rondo in the direction of the Bulevar, correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you give us an indication of the furthest point eastward toward the Bulevar which the tank approached? How far down Liska Street did the tank advance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The tank came up to this point here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you put an X on that point, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: [marks]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The morning before this operation began, were you briefed about the operation at the Vinko Skrobo headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that there would be an operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, could we briefly go into private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified about mercenaries or foreigners who were members of your unit. Did any of them participate in the action on the day, the day of the tank, the day that we have been talking about where the tank arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: First of all, these were not mercenaries. These were HVO soldiers, just like we were. And some of them did take part in the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I believe you've just it testified a minute ago that before you were down at the front line, at that position behind the wall in front of the health centre, before that, did you -- were you at the headquarters of the Vinko Skrobo up toward Kalemova Street?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. We were up there and then we came to the front line and we then waited for further instructions there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know someone named Dinko Knezovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he involved in transporting prisoners from the Heliodrom to the Vinko Skrobo headquarters? Was that one of his tasks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't one of his tasks but he went to fetch them on two or three occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall if he went to fetch any prisoners on this day, the day of this tank operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: No. He did not go. And there were no prisoners anywhere nearby, near the command, near the headquarters or near the front line.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke in your testimony about other prisoners who stayed around the headquarters, fixing cars and the people who volunteered. Were they at the headquarters on this day? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know. I did not see them, and I was at the front line so I couldn't say that I saw them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know, sir, that during the same period of time, prisoners were being taken to work in confrontation lines throughout the city, including Santiceva Street, just to the north of you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know that prisoners were being taken to work for other units in other parts of town, such as Santiceva Street, during this period of the summer and fall of 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The conditions and the circumstances, the tasks, of the prisoners who came to your headquarters were much more pleasant than, say, working on the confrontation line in Santiceva Street. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was generally the same group of prisoners, the same individuals, who came and worked around the headquarters of the Vinko Skrobo, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were some of these people perhaps former friends or still friends with Mr. Martinovic, perhaps had some sort of a friendship or a relation before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know that. I can't tell you about that. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could we briefly go into private session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one last couple of questions, Mr. President, and I will finish before today's recess. I've got a new exhibit, it's a photograph. We don't have it marked but perhaps we could just have it marked and show it to the witness. While that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You have to show this photograph to the Defence counsel first.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, I wasn't informed, but I can see this exhibit, and I have no objections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you testified -- I had the impression that you know a little something about tanks so I just wanted to show it this to you. Does this -- can you tell us the model of the tank that's shown on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: This is JNA tank, T-55.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you put it on the ELMO, please, so that we can all see it?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, just so we are clear, this is not a photograph of the tank on the day in question. This is just a photograph that was obtained from a different source. My question is whether, in fact, this is the model of the tank that you've testified about so far today, in connection with the events of 17 September.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yes. This is the tank of this model, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When the tank approached the Bulevar, would it be correct to say that there were not people on top of the turret as is shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Yeah, that's correct, because when the tank is going into combat operation, all the crew is inside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you don't know the answers, then tell us you don't know, but if you do know, and if you feel confident about saying so, can you indicate the area or areas where a person firing the tank shells would be positioned in the tank? What would be their vantage point and how would they see their target?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question? I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll try to clarify it. You testified that you heard that the sighting device had been shot so that they weren't able to fire any more shells. What would be the location of the firing or the sighting device on this tank, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: The sighting device of the tank is about here, and then the -- that's of the driver. And then above would be the sighting device of the tank. And here, there would be part of the tank, of the sighting equipment, and the periscope of the tank operator.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they would be inside the tank with the hatch closed, sighting their targets by using the periscope?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: In combat operations, that's how this is done, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Would you agree with me, sir, if I were to suggest to you that the height of the turret above the ground is 1.75 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time that the tank rolled down Liska Street into the position that you've marked on the photograph, from that point on the X, were there sandbags in front of the tank or behind the tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MQ
utterances.text: At that time, there were no sandbags because the tank went through the sandbags.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Stringer, for the sake of the record, would you please inform us about the number of that photo of the tank?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Exhibit 958, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, Witness, for coming here to give your evidence. When the usher pulls down the blinds, she will show you out of the room. We wish you pleasant journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, any documents to tender at this stag?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I am tendering as exhibit, first the name, the surname. That would be D2/48, I think. And then I'm not sure that's the right number. Yes, that will be/47. That will be name and surname. Then I'm tendering the map, D2/48, and I'm tendering the photograph, D2/49. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No objections, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Those three documents are admitted into evidence. Any documents on your side to tender, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We would tender the Exhibit 14.5 that was marked by the witness and then also the photograph of the tank that was Exhibit 958, and I think the other documents referred to are already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: How about P11.18?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, 11.18 also. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any objections, Mr. Par?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Those documents are admitted into evidence. And Mr. Par, do we have another witness for this week?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. We have another three witnesses who are here in The Hague. Tomorrow is Friday and I believe that tomorrow we could perhaps finish two of these witnesses, because their testimonies are shorter and then we would have one over for Monday. So that's what we estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much for the information. We will break now until tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
